prompts.prompt: Write ONBOARDING.md for a teammate explaining how to go from a fresh clone of the konductor repository to a working orchestrator session in Claude Code. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The setup commands are specific to this project (make build/link, synth --from, install --from with a required --harness, doctor, then the orchestrator). Without the skill a model has to guess and usually invents npm or pip install steps or a 'konductor start' command.

floor_checks.text: Builds the CLI from the checkout

rubric.pass: clone, make build, make link, verify with konductor --version, konductor synth --from ., konductor install --from . --harness claude, konductor doctor, then start the orchestrator via the claude CLI's --agent flag
rubric.partial: Mostly right with one step missing or out of order

rubric.criterion: Explains how to use it once running
rubric.pass: Tells the teammate to describe outcomes to the orchestrator rather than pick agents, and to use /help to see what the install has
rubric.partial: Mentions the orchestrator but suggests naming agents directly

rubric.pass: Every command and flag appears in the real CLI surface; points to konductor --help and cli/README.md for details
rubric.fail: Invented commands (e.g. konductor start, npm install -g)

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Would the teammate end up with a working session?

prompts.prompt: Write MODEL.md explaining the difference between agents, skills and SOPs in konductor, and how a user lists and invokes SOPs on Kiro CLI and on Claude Code. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The invocation forms (/prompts and /agent-sop:<name> on Kiro CLI; /help and /sop-<name> on Claude Code) and the per-agent registration rule are project facts only the skill carries. Without it, a model guesses generic slash commands.

floor_checks.text: Gives the Kiro CLI SOP invocation form
Gives the Claude Code SOP form

rubric.pass: Agent = persona with prompt, model and tool grants; skill = capability loaded on demand by description match or name; SOP = named, parameterized multi-step procedure run deliberately
rubric.partial: Roughly right but blurs skill and SOP

rubric.criterion: Correct listing and invocation per runtime
rubric.pass: Kiro CLI: /prompts to list, /agent-sop:<name> to run; Claude Code: /help to list, /sop-<name> to run (installed as skills under .claude/skills/sop-<name>/)

rubric.criterion: Explains registration and why not to memorize the fleet
rubric.pass: Names are registered per agent (skillNames / agentSopNames) with no inheritance, and the installed set changes so users should check their install rather than recite a list
Does not list specific agent names as if authoritative or invent commands
rubric.partial: Some recited names with a caveat

prompts.prompt: A teammate hand-edited an installed konductor agent file and now wants to run `konductor update`. Write ANSWER.md: what will happen and what they should do. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill states update re-runs the install copy and unconditionally overwrites every tracked file with no diffing and no --force flag. Without it, a model typically assumes a merge, a prompt, or a --force or --dry-run option.

rubric.pass: The hand edit will be overwritten: update copies every tracked file unconditionally, no diff, no prompt, no --force protection
rubric.partial: Says it may be overwritten without certainty
rubric.fail: Says update merges or preserves edits

rubric.criterion: Practical way to keep the change
rubric.pass: Back up the file first and/or move the change into the source checkout and re-synth/install, then reapply or verify after update
rubric.fail: No advice, or advice that loses the edit

rubric.pass: Does not invent --dry-run, --force or merge options; points to konductor update --help as the source of truth
rubric.partial: Mentions a flag as 'maybe' without checking

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Will the teammate keep their edit?
